schemes.label: Feed-in Tariffs
schemes.source: Ofgem Feed-in Tariffs Annual Report Scheme Year 15 (April 2024 to March 2025), Figure 3.3 "FIT scheme value, SY1-15" (PDF, feed_in_tariff_annual_report_sy15, Dec 2025). The report states the series grew every year from SY1 to SY11 (GBP 1,764m), fell for the first time in SY12 (GBP 1,575m), peaked at GBP 1,858m in SY14, and was GBP 1,844m in SY15, which fixes the year order of the charted values.

schemes.label: Climate Change Levy (electricity share) + Carbon Price Support
schemes.attribution_note: Electricity's share of CCL main-rate liabilities (HMRC's published commodity split of declarations) plus Carbon Price Support receipts, which fall wholly on electricity generation. Gas/solid-fuel main-rate CCL is excluded.
schemes.source: HMRC Environmental Taxes Bulletin (formerly Climate Change Levy and Carbon Price Floor Bulletin), March 2026 edition, tables ODS (2026_March_env_tabs_test.ods), Table 1b "CCL and CPF receipts and clearances data by calendar year". Value = electricity main-rate declared liabilities (the only commodity split HMRC publishes) plus estimated CPF receipts (CPS applies solely to fossil fuels used for electricity generation, so it is wholly electricity-attributable). Sums rounded down to the nearest GBP 0.1m.

schemes.label: Emissions trading (power-sector share of UK auction revenue)
schemes.attribution_note: Power-sector share of AUCTIONED allowance revenue only; free allocation excluded. Share taken as electricity generation's share of total verified covered emissions - a lower bound, since power receives no free allocation and so buys a larger share of auctioned allowances than its emissions share.
schemes.source: Auction revenue: 2012-2018 calendar-year sums of UK EUA auction results from the European Commission's UK Phase III Auction Platform Reports nos. 57 and 58 (ICE Futures Europe auctions on behalf of BEIS/DECC), converted from EUR at Bank of England annual average rates; 2019-2020 "EU ETS auction income" from the BEIS Annual Report and Accounts 2020-21 Trust Statement (FY2019-20 GBP 201.4m, FY2020-21 GBP 2,213.1m); 2021-2023 "UK ETS auction income" from the BEIS/DESNZ Annual Report and Accounts Trust Statements (FY2021-22 GBP 5,753,639k, FY2022-23 GBP 6,048,951k, FY2023-24 GBP 3,407,068k), attributed to the calendar year in which the financial year starts. 2024 uses the PUBLISHED CALENDAR-YEAR total instead - see calendar_year_revenue below. Power-sector share: from published UK ETS verified emissions (electricity generation / total covered); 2009-2020 a flat 0.5 estimate. See emissions_vintage below for the figures and their editions.

schemes.label: Transmission Network Use of System (attributed uplift)
schemes.attribution_note: Raw totals stored; attribution happens in the money model. Only the increase above the CPIH-indexed 2002-05 baseline (GBP 0.9bn/yr) is attributed to renewables, floored at zero.
schemes.source: 2013-2024: NESO TNUoS charging statements (total revenue), as compiled in David Turver's "TNUoS and BSUoS summary" workbook from NESO's Final TNUoS Tariffs publications. Calendar mapping is fiscal-year-ended-March minus one (the period starting April of the calendar year); validated because the 2022-24 calendar values reproduce our three independent NESO anchors exactly - "Final TNUoS Tariffs for 2023/24" (GBP 4,416.4m, our 2023) and "Final TNUoS Tariffs for 2024/25" (MAR Total Revenue GBP 4,188.5m, our 2024). 2002-2004: GBP 0.9bn/yr per the verified 2002-05 baseline (reference/baselines.yaml). Earliest intermediate years 2005-2012: REF April 2025 study Table 2 total-charge column (in parentheses), itself compiled from NESO/Ofgem charging statements - pending primary confirmation (not reached by the Turver/NESO series).

schemes.label: Balancing costs (BSUoS uplift)
schemes.attribution_note: Raw totals stored; attribution happens in the money model. Only the increase above the CPIH-indexed 2002-05 baseline (GBP 0.4bn/yr) is attributed, NET of wind constraint payments already counted in the direct layer, floored at zero.
schemes.source: 2005, 2011-2013: NAO "Electricity Balancing Services" (May 2014, HC 41, from Ofgem/National Grid data): total balancing costs recovered through BSUoS GBP 642m in 2005-06 rising to GBP 1,002m in 2013-14; 2011-12 plus 2012-13 expenditure totalled GBP 1,723m (split evenly here, the lower of NAO and REF figures). 2002-2004: GBP 0.4bn/yr per the verified 2002-05 baseline (reference/baselines.yaml). 2006-2010 and 2014-2016: REF April 2025 study Table 2 total-charge column, pending confirmation against National Grid Monthly Balancing Services Summary archives.

corrections.figure_label: Emissions trading (power-sector share of UK auction revenue)
cause: The power sector's share of UK ETS emissions was taken as 30.4 of 85.6 MtCO2e. No published source gives 30.4 Mt: DESNZ's Functioning of the UK carbon market, 2024 (section 7.3) gives 29,484,524 tCO2e of 85,634,344, a share of 34.43% rather than 35.51%.

The 2022 denominator was likewise held as 110.0 Mt against a published 110.6 Mt, and 2023 was held at the 2023 report's 37.1 Mt after DESNZ restated it to 36,084,695 tCO2e. Revenue for 2024 now uses the published calendar-year auction total (£2,564,090,000 across 25 auctions) instead of converting a financial-year accounts figure. 2022 and 2023 also move, to £2,635.4m and £1,270.7m.
Found during routine checking of this site's figures against primary sources.

The series was built from NESO's Daily Balancing Costs dataset, which is a breakdown of balancing-mechanism and ancillary spend rather than the balancing cost recovered through BSUoS. Its columns sum to 23-39% below the outturn in NESO's Annual Balancing Costs Report in every year from 2018-19 (2023-24: £1,824m against £2,455m).

Two faults compounded. The dataset is narrower than the charge it was taken to represent; and the fetched series began on 1 April 2017, so the published 2017 figure covered nine months rather than twelve. Together they produced a 63% fall between raw 2016 (£1,200m) and raw 2017 (£439m). On the corrected basis the missing quarter accounts for 26% of calendar 2017, and the narrow basis understated the nine months actually fetched by a further 52%.

The series now reads NESO's settled BSUoS charge data: the half-hourly charge to 31 March 2023, and actual BSUoS cost thereafter, the fixed-tariff reform of April 2023 having broken the identity between what users are charged and what balancing costs. Both are on the gross BSUoS basis, matching the pre-2017 history and the £0.4bn/yr 2002-05 baseline. The corrected series runs 1.10-1.23 times the Annual Balancing Costs Report outturn with no step at either seam, and the 2016-to-2017 change is +3.2%.
The combined total in 2024 prices rises from £228.6bn to £239.9bn; the published headline of over £220 billion is unchanged. The error understated the cost, so the correction raises the figure.
Found while checking this site's own figures against primary sources during a review of a Renewable Energy Foundation paper.

corrections.figure_label: Headline total — how it was described
corrections.now: stated as including estimated indirect costs
cause: The headline counter includes the estimated indirect costs — network and balancing charges, carbon pricing and the capacity levy — whenever the 'Include indirect costs' switch is on, which is its default. The sentence printed directly beneath the figure named only the four direct schemes: the Renewables Obligation, Contracts for Difference, Feed-in Tariffs and constraint payments. Those four are £132.3bn of the £229.2bn shown. The remaining £96.9bn, about two pounds in every five, is the estimated indirect layer, and the caption did not say so.

The figure itself was not wrong, and the switch controlling it was visible and correctly labelled. What was wrong was the description: a reader who took the caption as the definition of the number — the ordinary reading — would have understood a measured total of payments to generators, when more than two fifths of it is an attributed estimate. This site's own rule is that estimated and measured money must never be presented as the same thing.

The cause was a display change of 18 June 2026. Two sentences that did carry the disclosure — 'including estimated indirect costs' above the figure, and 'plus estimated indirect system costs' below it — were written correctly but hidden by the stylesheet of the new page design, which replaced them with the shorter caption. From 23 June 2026, when the indirect switch began defaulting to on, the combined figure was published under a description of the direct schemes alone. It stood for 99 days.

The caption now names the indirect costs in both states of the switch, and links to the attribution method. The methodology page has also been corrected: it stated that indirect costs were never folded into the headline, which was true of an earlier design and not of the one shipped.
Found while reconciling this site against a review of a Renewable Energy Foundation paper.

indirect_crosscheck.json.ref_source: REF, "UK Renewable Electricity Subsidy Totals 2002 to the Present Day", April 2025, Table 2 (and Capacity column)

components.note: REF counts total CCL receipts (OBR series, all fuels); we count electricity's share of main-rate receipts plus Carbon Price Support. Our figure is expected to be lower.
REF counts total ETS receipts (OBR series, all sectors); we count only the power-sector share of auctioned allowance revenue. Our figure is expected to be much lower.

We net off direct constraint payments and REF does not, which pulls our figure down; but our gross BSUoS base is larger than REF's stated total charge (calendar 2023 GBP 3.26bn against REF's fiscal 2023/24 GBP 2.9bn), which pushes it up by more. The two effects leave us slightly above REF rather than below. Before the 30 Sep 2026 basis correction our base was understated and we landed below REF, so this note previously read "our figure is expected to be lower" - that expectation no longer holds and the agreement within 4% is now the like-for-like result.

components.note: Both series sum the same April-March Ofgem scheme years, so the gap is not a calendar-vs-fiscal timing difference. Ours uses Ofgem's published FIT scheme value (generation + export + qualifying costs); REF's lower figure appears to use a narrower payments basis, plus rounding to GBP 0.1bn. The residual is a definitional difference and is not yet fully reconciled with REF.

REF's CfD line covers renewable generators including biomass; ours is CfD-renewables, which likewise already includes biomass (Drax and the like). CfD-nuclear contributes nothing in this window - Hinkley Point C payments begin in 2025.
REGO certificate costs are excluded from the Clock entirely (listed under "What is not included").
REF counts total CCL receipts (OBR series, all fuels); we count electricity's share of main-rate receipts plus Carbon Price Support.

REF does not net off direct constraint payments; we do, to avoid double-counting against our constraints line. Our gross BSUoS base is nonetheless larger than REF's, so on the full window we still land below REF but by less than the netting alone implies.
REF counts total ETS receipts (OBR series, all sectors); we count only the power-sector share of auctioned allowance revenue.

The 2022 denominator was likewise held as 110.0 Mt against a published 110.6 Mt, and 2023 was held at the 2023 report's 37.1 Mt after DESNZ restated it to 36,084,695 tCO2e. Revenue for 2024 now uses the published calendar-year auction total (£2,564,090,000 across 25 auctions) instead of converting a financial-year accounts figure. 2022 and 2023 also move, to £2,635.4m and £1,270.7m. 2026-09-30,bsuos,Balancing costs (BSUoS uplift),£12.54bn cumulative (£1.62bn/yr run-rate),£22.85bn cumulative (£3.39bn/yr run-rate),"The series was built from NESO's Daily Balancing Costs dataset, which is a breakdown of balancing-mechanism and ancillary spend rather than the balancing cost recovered through BSUoS. Its columns sum to 23-39% below the outturn in NESO's Annual Balancing Costs Report in every year from 2018-19 (2023-24: £1,824m against £2,455m). Two faults compounded. The dataset is narrower than the charge it was taken to represent; and the fetched series began on 1 April 2017, so the published 2017 figure covered nine months rather than twelve. Together they produced a 63% fall between raw 2016 (£1,200m) and raw 2017 (£439m). On the corrected basis the missing quarter accounts for 26% of calendar 2017, and the narrow basis understated the nine months actually fetched by a further 52%. The series now reads NESO's settled BSUoS charge data: the half-hourly charge to 31 March 2023, and actual BSUoS cost thereafter, the fixed-tariff reform of April 2023 having broken the identity between what users are charged and what balancing costs. Both are on the gross BSUoS basis, matching the pre-2017 history and the £0.4bn/yr 2002-05 baseline. The corrected series runs 1.10-1.23 times the Annual Balancing Costs Report outturn with no step at either seam, and the 2016-to-2017 change is +3.2%. The combined total in 2024 prices rises from £228.6bn to £239.9bn; the published headline of over £220 billion is unchanged. The error understated the cost, so the correction raises the figure. Found while checking this site's own figures against primary sources during a review of a Renewable Energy Foundation paper.",Richard Lyon
